title: SO-F-03.4 Contribution signature and two-step admission: a signed, scoped, classified contribution built on the operation envelope, admission into the node's own operation log, replay refused across restarts, and authority checked apart from the signature
request: Version 4 of this spec, which supersedes SO-F-03.3 (signed as contract k-so-f-03-3-contribution-s-0bb27e, built in pull request #358; the SO-F-03.3 spec file is unchanged and stays on record, and the manifest and RECONCILIATION mark it superseded by this spec). Unsigned: a delta proposed for red-team review in pull request #374. Reason: the red-team review of pull request #374 and the owner decision of 1 Nov 2026 that the replay sequence is per sender and scope, one Admission per scope. SO-F-03.3 keeps the high-water mark per sender across all scopes, in memory, read from the log once when the Admission is made and never again. Two things follow, both read and run in a scratch script outside the repository at 042d727: (1) a second Admission over the same log, even a bare new Admission(...) that nothing else knows of, has a stale mark and admits a sequence that another Admission has already admitted, so the log holds it twice; (2) with one Admission per scope over one log, whether a sequence is a replay depends on when each Admission was made, live and after a restart. Changes from SO-F-03.3: (1) the mark is kept per sender and scope; highWater(sender, scope) takes the scope, which defaults to the scope the Admission holds, so every existing call highWater(sender) keeps its meaning; the scope of a stored record is the scope in its stored envelope (rec.data.envelope.extension.contribution.scope), and a stored record that has no usable scope or no usable sequence moves no mark and throws nothing; the key is a structured pair of the sender and the scope and never a plain join of its parts, so two pairs whose joined text would be equal keep their own marks. (2) The Admission reads the log again, incrementally: before the replay check and in highWater it reads with the log's own iterate({ fromSeq }) from the record after the last one it has read, and it does not read at all when the seq of the log has not moved; an append of its own moves the cursor to that record only when its seq is the last seq read plus 1, the very next record, and otherwise the cursor stays where it was and the next read starts at the last seq read plus 1, so that a record another Admission appended in between is still read (a cursor that jumped to every own append would skip it and admit a sequence twice); a log with no numeric seq is read from the record after the last one read each time. That closes both the second Admission over the same log, bare or not, and the order dependence, at the root. (3) Two criteria pin the scope: a message replayed into a different scope is refused (its scope is inside the signed bytes, so the Admission of the other scope refuses it at the signature step), beside the check that the same message again in its own scope is a replay. (4) The reason of the code external_failed, which a hook that throws gets, is fixed text and no longer repeats the message of the throw, which can carry text of the payload; the code, the step and the event are unchanged, and the test at test/federation-admission.test.mjs:320 asserts only ok, step and code, so it stays green. (5) The text that still says per sender is brought in line: docs/FEDERATION.md (the field table row of the sequence and the paragraph after the two steps), docs/schemas/contribution-v1.json (the description of sequence), the head comment of src/engine/federation/contribution.mjs, the head comment of src/engine/federation/admission.mjs and docs/OPERATION-ENVELOPE.md (the list of what other contracts add), by edits to comments and prose only; a command criterion fails on any of the stale phrases and requires the new one in each file. Criterion 2 of SO-F-03.3 (its statement says the per-sender high-water mark) is superseded by the criterion that takes its place here, at the same position and with the same named test; every other criterion of SO-F-03.3 is carried with its statement verbatim and its command unpiped (no tail), per the red-team note on pull request #374. The tests those criteria select (SO-F-03 AC02, AC03, AC04, AC12 and AC13 of test/federation-admission.test.mjs) pass as they are: none admits one sender in two scopes over one log (checked by running test/federation-admission.test.mjs and test/membership.test.mjs, 29 tests, against the change in a scratch copy of 042d727 outside the repository; all pass). BASE: SO-F-03.3, merged by pull request #358 (on main). src/engine/federation/admission.mjs, src/engine/federation/contribution.mjs and test/federation-admission.test.mjs on main are the same files as at 042d727, the commit I read and ran; the tests of the new criteria use only the helpers inside test/federation-admission.test.mjs and files on main, so their red check runs against main. PRECONDITION, CHECKED: the scope is bound in the signed bytes. At 042d727, contributionMessage in src/engine/federation/contribution.mjs (line 67) is the text that is signed: a header line and the canonical text of the whole envelope without its content hash and without the signature, so extension.contribution.scope, the sequence, the subject and the node (origin.node) are all inside the signed bytes; signContribution (line 85) signs that text. No test of SO-F-03 proves the scope part (the test at test/federation-admission.test.mjs:226 to 228 proves it for the payload hash only), so a criterion of SO-F-03.4 does. If the signed text ever stops covering the scope, a mark per sender and scope is not safe and the stop rules apply. Not changed: the constructor and its options, the steps and their order, every code, the two event types (federation.admitted and federation.rejected) and the keys of the stored record, and the synchronous return of Admission.admit; the only text of a record that changes is the reason of external_failed; no store and no event type is added, and the log is the only store. docs/FEDERATION.md, in the paragraph of the section Contribution and admission that says the sequence is held against the high-water mark of the sender, is rewritten to say per sender and scope, and that the log is read again when it has moved (the other files of change (5) are listed there). Wherever the text of SO-F-03.3 that follows says a per-sender sequence or a per-sender high-water mark (its request and criteria 1 and 2), read it as per sender and scope for the mark; the sequence field of the envelope is unchanged and is the number the mark is held against. SO-F-04A and SO-F-04B depend on this version, which is built first. MERGE ORDER of the three specs of pull request #374, which touch the same files. Spec pull requests: #374 changes contracts/scope-one/manifest.json, docs/scope-one/RECONCILIATION.md and docs/scope-one/WBS.md the way every spec-only pull request does, by adding rows and, for a superseded contract, two fields, so it and the other open spec pull request that does the same (SO-F-09.3, #373) take a plain merge of main in whichever order they land, keeping both sets of rows; no spec depends on that order. BUILD ORDER: SO-F-03.4 first (it needs only main, where #358 landed SO-F-03.3), then SO-F-04A, then SO-F-04B (both need pull request #368, SO-F-04, merged), one after the other and never in parallel, because all three edit src/engine/federation/admission.mjs, and they edit docs/FEDERATION.md, docs/MODULES.md and test/helpers/** as well: SO-F-03.4 changes the mark and the log read and the reason of external_failed, SO-F-04A adds composeExternal, SO-F-04B adds AdmissionSet and one registration in the constructor; the one built later merges the one built earlier before it is built on, and SO-F-04A and SO-F-04B depend on SO-F-03.4 in the manifest for that reason. SIGN ORDER: the same, SO-F-03.4, then SO-F-04A, then SO-F-04B. The request text of SO-F-03.3 follows unchanged. Version 3 of this spec, which supersedes SO-F-03.2 (signed as contract k-so-f-03-2-contribution-s-bc1be8, merged by pull request #355; the SO-F-03.2 spec file is unchanged and stays on record, and the manifest and RECONCILIATION mark it superseded by this spec). Reason: owner delegation, 1 Nov 2026: pull request #358 carries commit cfcc2db, which replaces the stale 'under review in pull request #224' line at README.md:195 with the current state of federation, and that line stays; README.md is in no scope of SO-F-03.2. SO-F-03.3 adds README.md to the scope of T1 and changes no requirement, criterion or other scope entry. Version 2 of this spec, which supersedes SO-F-03 (signed as contract k-so-f-03-contribution-sig-2ba083, version 2; the SO-F-03 spec file is unchanged and stays on record, and the manifest and RECONCILIATION mark it superseded by this spec). Decided under owner delegation, 1 Nov 2026: build PG-04.1 WP04-01 and WP04-02 first, then this contract, because it defines the signature and admission block of the operation envelope that PG-04.1 specifies. Changes from SO-F-03: (1) PG-04.1 is a predecessor beside SO-F-01 and SO-F-02; (2) the envelope specification docs/OPERATION-ENVELOPE.md, the implementation src/engine/envelope.mjs and the tests test/envelope.test.mjs are named in the scope of T1, so a reviewer reads them and a change to them after the review makes this spec stale (they are specified by PG-04.1 WP04-01 and WP04-02 and may not exist until those land). Every other requirement, criterion and scope entry is kept, including the guards that moved here from SO-F-11. Build layer of the Scope One programme, adapted from the fold of 30 Oct 2026 (fold id SO-F-03) and validated against memev main at d1c65ef. Contracts marked with a dagger are signed in the owner's vault and are not visible in this repository; they are cited by id only. Implements the design records SO-2.02 (Permission-aware knowledge access: retrieval governed by identity, project membership, classification, policy and jurisdiction); SO-2.03 (Provenance, retention and invalidation of organisational knowledge) (contracts/scope-one/specs). The decision record cites this contract by id and keeps only the gaps this one does not cover. Builds on signed vault contracts: MEM-145†. Memev contracts that land first: PG-04.1 (WP04-01, the envelope specification, and WP04-02, the envelope implementation and tests), SO-F-01, SO-F-02. Page: docs/FEDERATION.md comes from the federation architecture documentation (PR #223, branch docs/federation-architecture, not on main); until that merges, the first contract to need a page creates it with its Status section, labelled planned or architectural target, and the later ones extend it. Source in the fold: #222 section 13.7 (signed structured contributions; accountable admission) and #223 FEDERATION.md (state exchange with versioned contracts, provenance and defined reconciliation). Settled decisions this contract follows (owner decision 31 Oct 2026, docs/scope-one/DECISIONS.md): topology is local-first and the cloud is only a relay and a backup; every supported provider stands on equal footing and no work or tier depends on one; crdt-merge is reached only through the provider boundary of src/engine/merge.mjs (docs/EXTENSION-POINTS.md) and this contract adds no merge engine to the core; tiers follow docs/PRICING.md (Free core, Personal for up to 3 computers with no per-computer add-on, higher tiers by contacting us) with no Personal trial; the git backup keeps running every few minutes (sync.interval_min). Memory authority: ADR 7 (memory and project-state authority) is proposed in PR #325 and is not decided here; this contract cites it and the local-first decision, and keeps one store under the vault with no second database. Provenance: adapted from the fold of 30 Oct 2026. Changes: (1) converted from the vault task format to the memev spec format (named tests run as red-green checks on the own test file of the contract; inline regular expression flags became the flags key; hygiene and decision verifiers became commands or doc checks). (2) removed fold-only fields and the owner-decision marker field, reworded the stop rule that named a patent, and made the text pass the leak scan. (3) Duplicate removed: the operation envelope of PG-04.1 (docs/OPERATION-ENVELOPE.md, src/engine/envelope.mjs, test/envelope.test.mjs) is the one envelope. The fold defined a second envelope and the same test name; this contract now adds only the signature and admission block (docs/schemas/contribution-v1.json), the per-sender sequence and the rejected event, and builds on PG-04.1. (4) src/engine/agentid-bind.mjs added to scope: its signMessage is private and it verifies only role bindings, so federation code had no generic verify through the same ssh-keygen path. A namespaced verify is exported there, so src/engine/federation imports no child_process. The signature uses a namespace distinct from the binding namespace, so a role-binding signature cannot be replayed as a contribution signature. (5) Replay refusal must survive a restart: devices.mjs NonceCache is a 10-minute in-memory cache, so the per-sender sequence high-water mark is persisted through the operation log and rebuilt on open (the restart-proof replay rule of SR-1.03 is the pattern; it is cited, not copied). (6) Absorbed from the dropped SO-F-11: a guard that src/engine/federation imports no child_process, net, http, https or dgram module. (7) The fold docs heading ## Contribution envelope becomes ## Contribution and admission, so it does not suggest a second envelope.

tasks.description: State may cross a boundary only as a contribution the receiving node can verify and judge. This contract defines the signature and admission block of the operation envelope of PG-04.1 and the node's own admission: verify the signature (the role key of MEM-145 through the same ssh-keygen path, offline), check authority and policy for the scope and classification, then append; a failed step records a rejected event in the vault's operation log through the OpLog API and appends nothing of the payload. Replay is refused through a sequence per sender and scope whose high-water mark is persisted through the operation log, so it survives a restart (the restart rule of SR-1.03), and every Admission reads the log again when it has moved, from the record after the last one it read, so that no two Admissions over one log admit one sequence. A signature proves a key signed; authority is a separate check. The external admission service of SO-F-08 runs before this step when configured. The classification field's values are constrained later by the classification schema of SO-F-05.

criteria.statement: a contribution is an operation envelope (PG-04.1) that carries subject, scope, a classification string whose values the classification schema of SO-F-05 constrains later, schema version, causal context, provenance, payload hash, a per-sender sequence and a signature made with the role key of MEM-145 through the same ssh-keygen path, in a namespace distinct from the role-binding namespace, and verified offline; the schema docs/schemas/contribution-v1.json defines only the signature and admission block, not a second envelope; the validator accepts the fixtures and refuses a missing field

stop_rules: Stop and post BLOCKED when a criterion cannot pass without weakening a test, skipping a test or relaxing an assertion.
Stop and ask when the work would name a client product, a person, a server or a seat in repository text; the client names live in docs/CLIENTS.md only.
Stop when the work would add a runtime dependency, a model call, a network call at install or start, a second store for project state, or any reporting that is not opt-in and off by default.
Stop when the work would move convergence logic into the core, vendor the engine, or add a merge engine beside the provider boundary of src/engine/merge.mjs.

Stop when the work would implement a federation, replication, trust, admission or computation feature beyond the specification, schema, validator and conformance test the contract names; the product keeps the planned label on it.

Stop and ask when the signed text of a contribution no longer covers extension.contribution.scope (contributionMessage of src/engine/federation/contribution.mjs, or the envelope, changed so that the scope is outside the signed bytes), or when the work would change either to make a test pass, beyond the comment at the head of contribution.mjs: a mark per sender and scope is safe only while the scope is signed.

Stop and ask when the work would change the constructor or its options, a step or the order of the steps, a code, an event type or the stored record of the Admission (the reason of external_failed apart), make Admission.admit asynchronous, or edit a test of SO-F-03 or SO-F-04 to make the change pass.

Stop and ask when the work would read the log other than through the iterate of the OpLog API, keep the mark anywhere but in memory rebuilt from the log, add a store, a file or an event type, or add a second guard in the constructor: the test AC04 of SO-F-03 builds a second Admission for a held scope and must keep passing.
